Devender Joshi & Ors vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 8
August, 2025
 $~40

 Devender Joshi & Ors.

entities.text: High Court Of Delhi At New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Through: Mr. Manoj, Mr. Sumit Bansal a
 Mr. Balram Sharma, Advs.
 versus
 State Nct Of Delhi And Anr .....

Resp
 Through: Mr. Satish Kumar, App for Sta
 Si Satish Kumar Ps Mangol Puri
 Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Ajay Digpaul
1. Exemption allowed subject to all just exceptions.
2. The application stands disposed of.

1. By way of present application, the petitioners seek exemption from filing the no-objection certificate/affidavit of respondent no. 2.
2.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that respondent no. 2 is not coming forward to sign the no-objection certificate despite there being a settlement agreement between the parties.
Owing to this, they are unable to file her affidavit filed in the present petition.
3. Issue notice.
Learned APP for State, who appears on advance notice, accepts notice.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 12/08/2025 at 22:05:41 4.
Issue notice to respondent no. 2 through all permissible modes on filing PF within one week.

The petitioners seek quashing of FIR No. 816/2016 registered at Police Station Mangolpuri, Delhi,
for the offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
7. Issue notice.
Learned APP for State, who appears on advance notice, accepts notice.

9. In view of the mandate of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jagjeet Singh & Ors. vs. Ashish Mishra @
Monu & Anr., 2022 9 SCC 321, the complainant/victim is entitled to be heard in the present proceedings.

entities.text:
Jagjeet Singh & Ors. vs. Ashish Mishra @
Monu & Anr., 2022 9 SCC 321
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, let intimation be sent by the Investigating Officer to the complainant/victim informing them that they are entitled to be heard in the present proceedings,
for which they may remain present (either in-person or via video-conferencing) or be represented on the next date.
10. Let proof of service of intimation be placed on record before the next date.
11.
AJAY DIGPAUL, J AUGUST 8, 2025 gs/av
